selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: In the First Warning, what wrong idea makes the nafs feel bored with prayer?
questions.answer: It acts as if life will go on for a very long time and never end.

questions.question: What questions are asked to remind the nafs that life is not guaranteed?
questions.answer: It is asked whether it has proof that it will even live until next year or even tomorrow.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the truth about a person’s life in this world?
questions.answer: Life is short and is quickly passing away.

questions.question: How much time out of a full day is described as being spent on worship?
questions.answer: One hour out of twenty-four.

questions.question: How is this act of worship described?
questions.answer: It is described as beautiful, easy, pleasant, and full of mercy.

questions.question: What great benefit does this worship help a person gain?
questions.answer: It helps a person reach the real happiness of the everlasting life.

questions.question: If a person truly understood life’s shortness, how would he feel about spending that hour in worship?
questions.answer: He would not feel tired of it; he would feel eager and pleased.

questions.question: What conclusion should a student draw from this warning?
questions.answer: A student should understand that prayer is a wise and worthwhile use of a little time in a short life.

questions.question: Who is being spoken to in the First Warning?
questions.answer: The speaker is addressing his own nafs, meaning the lower self.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the nafs by calling it unhappy and asking strong questions?
questions.answer: It suggests that the nafs is thinking wrongly and needs correction.

questions.question: Why does the nafs complain about worship?
questions.answer: It complains because it imagines it will stay in the world forever and keep enjoying worldly life.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the future of our lives?
questions.answer: It says we have no certain guarantee even for tomorrow.

questions.question: Why is it unwise to delay worship?
questions.answer: It is unwise because life may end soon, so a person should not act as if there will always be more time.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about daily time and worship?
questions.answer: It teaches that giving a small part of the day to Allah’s service is very reasonable.

questions.question: How does the passage connect worship with the next life?
questions.answer: It says worship is a way to gain true joy in the everlasting life.

questions.question: What is the first big point made in this warning about human life?
questions.answer: Human life is not forever and can end sooner than people expect.

questions.question: What kind of proof does the passage say the nafs does not have?
questions.answer: It does not have certain proof that it will keep living into the future.

questions.question: What mistake does the nafs make about life in this world?
questions.answer: It wrongly assumes it will remain here for ongoing enjoyment.

questions.question: What happens when someone forgets that life is brief?
questions.answer: That person starts seeing worship as annoying instead of valuable.

questions.question: How much of the day is asked for this act of service?
questions.answer: Only a small portion of the day, one hour.

questions.question: Why is this amount of time presented as fair and reasonable?
questions.answer: Because it is a small amount of time for something very beneficial and meaningful.

questions.question: What words in the passage show that worship is not meant to harm us?
questions.answer: It is shown as gentle, good, and beneficial, not harsh.

questions.question: In this warning, what is the nafs forgetting about death?
questions.answer: It is forgetting that death may come before long and that no one has a promise of many more years.

questions.question: What does the passage say is happening to life right now?
questions.answer: It says life is already slipping away.
